finding.claim: OS command injection in /ping: unauthenticated req.query.host is concatenated into a shell command string passed to child_process.exec, which runs it through a shell. An attacker can append shell metacharacters (e.g. host=8.8.8.8;id or $(cmd)) to execute arbitrary commands, and the output is returned in the response.
finding.source: req.query.host (HTTP GET /ping query parameter, no authentication)

trace.note: host concatenated into the shell command string and passed to exec(), which spawns /bin/sh -c
command stdout is returned to the caller via res.send(out), so output is exfiltrated

finding.guards_checked: No input validation or allowlist/regex on host; no authentication or middleware on the app; no escaping; not using execFile with an argv array. Not a decoy: the /version and /uptime handlers use constant commands, but /ping includes user input. Also, host could start with '-' for option injection even without a shell.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 passes "ping -c 1 " + req.query.host to exec() (a shell) with no validation, auth, or middleware in the file, and tools.js:11 returns stdout, so an anonymous caller can inject commands. The output is only returned when ping exits 0, so the injected command must still leave a zero exit status, e.g. `;id` works because the shell's exit status comes from the last command.
